description.summary: Privileged wayland protocol for capturing gamepad devices

protocol.description:
To start receiving gamepad input events, a client must first bind the global interface cosmic_gamepad_manager, which will be used to request a seat-specific object, using get_gamepad_seat.
A cosmic_gamepad_seat object is used by the compositor to notify the client of connected controllers, via the gamepad_available event. The cosmic_gamepad object contained in that event is then used to send actual input events.
Which surface currently holds the focus of the gamepad, and therefore receives input events from that controller, is maintained by the compositor and communicated to the client with the enter and leave events.
The client can request to temporarily get exclusive access to a cosmic_gamepad object via the grab request. The returned cosmic_gamepad_grab object will indicate a successful grab through its sucess event. If successful any input event will only be forwarded to the cosmic_gamepad object regardless of focus until the grab is volentary revoked or the compositor ends it.
Clients should watch for the wp_gamepad.removed event, which indicates a device was unplugged. If the same device is then replugged, it results in a new wp_gamepad_seat.gamepad_available event and a new wp_gamepad object. Gamepads can be identified across hotplug events by their unique ID, sent in the wp_gamepad.device_info event.

interface.name: zcosmic_gamepad_manager_v1
interface.description: An object that provides access to connected gamepads.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the cosmic_gamepad_manager object.
The objects created from this object are unaffected and should be destroyed separately.

request.name: get_gamepad_seat
request.description: Get the cosmic_gamepad_seat object for a given seat. This object provides access to all gamepads in this seat.

arg.name: seat
arg.summary: The wl_seat object for which to receive controller input

interface.name: zcosmic_gamepad_seat_v1

description.summary: manager object for gamepads attached to a seat

interface.description: An object providing access to the gamepads available on this seat. After binding to this interface, the compositor sends available gamepad through gamepad_available event.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the cosmic_gamepad_seat object.
The objects created from this object are unaffected and should be destroyed separately.

event.name: gamepad_available
event.description: This event is sent whenever a gamepad becomes available on this seat.

interface.name: zcosmic_gamepad_v1
interface.description:
This interface represents a physical gamepad currently connected to the system.
Upon binding to the interface, the compositor will advertise the properties of the gamepad through the *_capability and device_info event.
Input events are grouped by the zcosmic_gamepad_v1.frame events. All events received before the frame event should be considered part of the same hardware state change.

event.name: button_capability

description.summary: advertises the availability of a particular button

event.description: Send to notify the client that a particular button event can be produced by this device. All capability events are send before the device_info event.

event.name: axis_capability

description.summary: advertises the availability of a particular button

event.description: Send to notify the client that a particular axis event can be produced by this device. All capability events are send before the device_info event.

event.name: touchpad_capability

description.summary: advertises the availability of a particular touchpad

event.description: Send to notify the client that a particular touchpad event can be produced by this device. All capability events are send before the device_info event.

enum.name: theme
enum.description: Each vendor uses a different set of glyph on its controller's buttons.

event.name: device_info
event.description:
Information about the gamepad. The name and uniq values are UTF-8 strings, the uniq value should not be NULL.
This event marks the end of the device initialization sequence and MUST be send after all capability events.

event.name: enter
event.description: Notification that the gamepad is focused on a given surface.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the enter event

event.name: leave
event.description: Notification that the gamepad is no longer focused on the given surface.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial number of the leave event

enum.name: button
enum.description: Describes the source of a button event.

enum.name: button_state
enum.description: Describes the physical state of a button on the gamepad.

entry.name: released
entry.summary: the input source is not pressed

event.name: button
event.description:
Describes the gamepad button source press and release notification.
The time arguments is a timestamp in microseconds granularity with an unknown base of the moment of the state changes

arg.name: time_hi
arg.summary: high 32 bits of a 64 bits timestamp with microsecond granularity

arg.name: time_lo
arg.summary: low 32 bits of a 64 bits timestamp with microsecond granularity

event.name: pressure
event.description:
Describes gamepad button source pressure notification, expressed with a value varying between 0.0 and 1.0, with 0.0 being the neutral state.
The time arguments is a timestamp in microseconds granularity with an unknown base of the moment of the state changes

arg.name: value
arg.summary: trigger value in the 0 to 1 range

arg.name: time_hi
arg.summary: high 32 bits of a 64 bits timestamp with microsecond granularity

arg.name: time_lo
arg.summary: low 32 bits of a 64 bits timestamp with microsecond granularity

enum.name: axis
enum.description: Describes the source of an axis event.

event.name: axis
event.description:
Describes gamepad axis position notification.
Thumbstick axis value varies from -1.0 to 1.0.
The time arguments is a timestamp in microseconds of the moment of the state changes

arg.name: value
arg.summary: axis value in the -1 to 1 range

arg.name: time_hi
arg.summary: high 32 bits of a 64 bits timestamp with microsecond granularity

arg.name: time_lo
arg.summary: low 32 bits of a 64 bits timestamp with microsecond granularity

enum.name: touchpad
enum.description: Describes the source of an touchpad event.

event.name: touchpad
event.description:
Describes gamepad touchpad position notification.
Touchpad values varies from -1.0 to 1.0.
The time arguments is a timestamp in microseconds of the moment of the state changes

arg.name: x
arg.summary: x axis value in the -1 to 1 range

arg.name: y
arg.summary: y axis value in the -1 to 1 range

arg.name: time_hi
arg.summary: high 32 bits of a 64 bits timestamp with microsecond granularity

arg.name: time_lo
arg.summary: low 32 bits of a 64 bits timestamp with microsecond granularity

event.name: frame

description.summary: end of a gamepad event sequence

event.description:
Indicates the end of a set of events that logically belong together. A client is expected to accumulate the data in all events within the frame before proceeding
All wp_gamepad_v1 events before a wp_gamepad_v1.frame event belong together.

request.name: grab

description.summary: request exclusive access to this gamepad

request.description:
Allows a client to request exclusive access to the underlying gamepad device.
Use the returned cosmic_gamepad_grab object to determine whether the grab was successful and/or modify the grab.
Trying to create multiple grab objects from the same gamepad will throw an already_grabbed protocol error. Previous cosmic_gamepad_grab objects need to be destroyed before a new one can be created.

event.name: removed
event.description: This event indicates that the controller is not available and no more events will follow. Upon receipt of this event, the client should immediately destroy the wp_gamepad object.

entry.name: already_grabbed
entry.summary: The gamepad obj already holds a grab.

interface.name: zcosmic_gamepad_grab_v1
interface.description:
An object that represents a grab of a cosmic_gamepad object.
Upon object creation the compositor will either send a success event if the grab was acquired or ended if it was denied.
The compositor might send ended at any later point to indicate that the grab was revoked by other means.
Destroying the object will also end the grab.

description.summary: The gamepad grab was successfully acquired.

event.name: ended

description.summary: The gamepad grab was denied or revoked.

event.description: This object will never receive any other event. A new grab object needs to be created to request a new grab.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the cosmic_gamepad_grab object.
This also ends the grab, if the object hasn't already received the ended event.
